The suit claims supervisors enforced a no-cellphone policy for Hispanic workers, while not enforcing it for others.Luis Penafiel, a former temp worker at the HelloFresh distribution center in Newark, New Jersey, from November 2021 to August 2023, and a plaintiff in the lawsuit claims that the working conditions began to deteriorate shortly after he was hired. “We started to realize that because we were Latinos, we were being forced to do all these kinds of duties. We started noting the discrimination,” he said.“We were afraid of punishment for complaining,” said Penafiel. “We want the authorities to listen to us and to realize the conditions that people are working under at these places.”According to the complaint, workers also alleged Hispanic workers were required to use a sign-out system in order to use the bathroom and that management policed the time they spent in the bathroom.“There were many times I had to hold it for hours because they would note down the time you went in,” Penafiel said. “I had to go to the clinic to a urologist because I started experiencing incontinence, as I had to hold it for a long time and ended up getting infections.”The lawsuit claimed non-Hispanic workers were allowed to use the bathroom whenever they wanted and for however long, often with the temp workers expected to fill in on work lines for direct hires when they took longer breaks or were using the bathroom.“On several occasions, a HelloFresh manager menaced Hispanic workers with a baseball bat to limit their time in the bathroom and force them to return to work on HelloFresh’s production line,” the complaint alleges. “HelloFresh’s bathroom policy was so restrictive that several Hispanic workers were forced to urinate on themselves and continue to work because their supervisors denied them permission to use the bathroom.”It added, “defendants’ bathroom policies were so restrictive that at least one member of the Hispanic Employee Class brought multiple pairs of underwear and fresh clothes to work because she was forced to urinate on herself on several occasions.”The complaint alleges instances of workers grabbing female employees’ body parts, having managers show workers pornography and photos of their genitalia, using loaves of bread and cucumbers to simulate sex acts, and regularly propositioning female workers for sex.“HelloFresh supervisors physically assaulted and battered several Hispanic employees during their employment at HelloFresh,” the lawsuit alleges, arguing the alleged assaults were done in view of other Hispanic employees with the intent of inducing fear of not following supervisors’ directives.The lawsuit described the alleged assaults as managers “physically beating workers”, “putting their hands around workers’ necks” and “screaming in workers’ ears”. The lawsuit also claimed workers were denied medical treatment for injuries sustained on the job.“When people would raise complaints about what they were suffering, what supervisors were doing, they were bounced back and forth between HelloFresh and the staffing agencies with very little resolution, so there was really no place for people to go with these complaints,” said Lauren Herman, an attorney with Make the Road New Jersey and one of the plaintiff’s attorneys in the lawsuit.“I think this lawsuit really illustrates what happens when you have effectively a two-tier labor force in the economy where we have the kind of aggressive immigration enforcement that’s happening right now that leaves people feeling so vulnerable that employers can hold their immigration status over their heads in this way and use that as a tool to exploit them,” said Michael Scimone, a partner at Outten and Golden representing the workers in the lawsuit.In court filings, the staffing agencies claimed HelloFresh offered direct employment to all workers, which the plaintiffs’ lawsuit disputes.Target Staffing’s attorneys argued in its motion to dismiss that the workers falsified their immigration documents and would not clear HelloFresh’s verification system. They also claimed no workers ever complained about the work environment at HelloFresh.The requests from each staffing agency to dismiss claims alleging violation of the New Jersey Human Trafficking Prevention, Protection, and Treatment Act were granted, though the judge allowed the plaintiffs to file an amended complaint to specify individually named plaintiffs or defendants.In December 2024, the US Department of Labor announced aninvestigation intoa different staffing agency at a HelloFresh facility in Illinois over allegations that migrant children were working at the facility. HelloFresh noted it terminated its relationship with the agency upon learning about the allegations.“Our frontline workforce is the foundation of our company, and ensuring a safe, fair, and respectful workplace is our highest priority,” HelloFresh said in an email. “HelloFresh maintains robust anti-discrimination and anti-harassment policies governed by our Employee Handbook andGlobal Code of Ethics. They are backed by mandatory training and multiple reporting channels, including a 24/7 confidential hotline for anonymous complaints. We take every concern seriously and remain fully dedicated to upholding a culture of integrity and accountability.”Explore more on these topicsBusinessNew JerseyDiscrimination at workFoodnewsShareReuse this content

title: Christiane Amanpour announces she’s leaving CNN after 43 years | CNN | The Guardian
description: Anchor’s departure not thought to be linked to company’s recent acquisition by David Ellison’s Skydance Media
Author: Jeremy Barr
Headline: Anchor’s departure not thought to be linked to company’s recent acquisition by David Ellison’s Skydance Media
Content: Christiane Amanpour in Bayeux, France, in 2018.Photograph: Charly Triballeau/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenChristiane Amanpour in Bayeux, France, in 2018.Photograph: Charly Triballeau/AFP/Getty ImagesCNNChristiane Amanpour announces she’s leaving CNN after 43 yearsAnchor’s departure not thought to be linked to company’s recent acquisition by David Ellison’s Skydance MediaJeremy BarrMon 19 Oct 2026 13.21 EDTFirst published on Mon 19 Oct 2026 12.36 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleChristiane Amanpour, one of CNN’s most decorated and venerated journalists, is leaving the network after 43 years, she said in a statement on Monday.Amanpour, who began working for the then-fledging network as an assistant on the international assignment desk in 1983 and is now its chief international anchor, will end her show Amanpour in May and leave the network at the end of June. She also hosts a show for PBS, Amanpour and Company, that will conclude at the end of this year.In the statement, Amanpour said she came to the decision to “separate” from the network “after many months of thought and a few sleepless nights”.“From my very first big exciting assignment covering the first Gulf war, to the horrors of the Bosnian war, Rwanda, Afghanistan, Ukraine and Iran and all the points in between, it’s the teams and the camaraderie that counted so much, as we together battled to seek the facts, the evidence and the humanity, so that CNN could always broadcast the truth about the world and to the world, without fear nor favor,” she wrote.She ended her statement by encouraging her CNN colleagues: “Remember: always be truthful, not neutral.”Amanpour, 68, has been open about her ongoing treatment for ovarian cancer, which she was diagnosed with in 2021.Her decision comes at a notable time for the network, which is now part of a larger media conglomerate called Skydance that is run by David Ellison, with heavy backing from Larry Ellison, his Trump-donor father and Oracle co-founder.Her exit is not thought to be specifically tied to the network’s new ownership, which is viewed skeptically by some CNN journalists because of its perceived closeness to the Trump administration. But, in her statement, Amanpour seemed to nod to concerns about the network’s future, saying that she “will always be rooting for CNN and maintaining its history of independent journalism”.She expanded on that commitment to independence in a taped message to viewers of her CNN International show on Monday afternoon.“You know that I’ve always been fiercely independent, and I will continue to be that for you for as long as I am here and beyond,” she said. “That’s especially important today as we face unprecedented pressures from all sides – political, financial, and also from the rising dangers in the field.”In his own memo, CNN’s CEO, Mark Thompson,who announced earlier this monththat he will be remaining with the merged company, thanked Amanpour “for 43 extraordinary years of remarkable journalism, loyalty and friendship”.“Christiane has thought carefully about this decision, and she and I have been discussing it for some months,” Thompson wrote. “Like so many CNNers who will hear the news today, I’m very sorry to see her go, but I’ve come to accept that this is the right time for her, both personally and professionally.”Amanpour said she will continue hosting her podcast, The Ex Files and that she “[looks] forward to interesting new projects down the line”.Explore more on these topicsCNNThe news on TVTV newsTelevisionTelevision industrynewsShareReuse this content

title: China’s economy grows faster than forecast after AI boom boosts exports | Chinese economy | The Guardian
description: Third-quarter GDP up by 4.5% compared with last year as industrial output is buoyed by electronics demand
Author: Julia Kollewe
Headline: Third-quarter GDP up by 4.5% compared with last year as industrial output is buoyed by electronics demand
Content: China’s economy has grown by 4.6% in the first nine months of the year.Photograph: Peter Parks/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenChina’s economy has grown by 4.6% in the first nine months of the year.Photograph: Peter Parks/AFP/Getty ImagesChinese economyChina’s economy grows faster than forecast after AI boom boosts exportsThird-quarter GDP up by 4.5% compared with last year as industrial output is buoyed by electronics demandJulia KolleweMon 19 Oct 2026 05.27 EDTLast modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 15.12 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRoaring exports lifted China’s economic growth in the third quarter of this year, with factory output growing much faster than consumer spending.China’s GDP grew by 4.5% year-on-year between July and September, the National Bureau of Statistics of China reported on Monday. The figures were better than economists had expected and up from the second quarter’s growth rate of 4.3%.China’s economy has now grown by 4.6% in the first nine months of the year, putting it on track to hit the government’s 2026 target of 4.5%-5% growth without extra stimulus measures.Industrial production rose 5.5% in September, up from 5.2% in August, while retail sales only increased 1.1%, up from 0.4%.Duncan Wrigley, the chief China economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics, said Beijing’s policymakers were likely to conclude that their efforts to stabilise headline growth in the third quarter were successful.“Headline industrial production rose in September partly as coalmines resumed operations after safety inspections prompted by a major accident. Manufacturing output growth remained robust at 6.0% year on year in September, buoyed up by stronger export demand for electronics, AI-related equipment and autos,” Wrigley said.“Hi-tech manufacturing output continues to outperform traditional sectors, as China climbs the value-added ladder,” Wrigley added.However, fixed-asset investment fell 7.2% over the first nine months, property investment tumbled by 20.6%, and infrastructure spending remained weak.Data last week showed that China’s exports surged by more than a third in September, lifted by a rise in shipments of electronics related to AI.“This pickup in GDP growth mainly reflects ongoing export strength on the global AI/tech boom, more than offsetting drags from the Iran conflict and ongoing weakness in domestic demand,” said analysts at ABN Amro.Explore more on these topicsChinese economyChinaEconomicsAsia PacificnewsShareReuse this content

title: AI firm Anthropic to commit 5% of shares to fund for ‘public good’ | Anthropic | The Guardian
description: The $48bn giveaway comes amid concerns about the tech and as the company prepares for a stock market listing
Author: Lauren Almeida
Headline: The $48bn giveaway comes amid concerns about the tech and as the company prepares for a stock market listing
Content: Anthropic was valued at $965bn in May when it raised $65bn in a funding round.Photograph: Dado Ruvić/ReutersView image in fullscreenAnthropic was valued at $965bn in May when it raised $65bn in a funding round.Photograph: Dado Ruvić/ReutersAnthropicAI firm Anthropic to commit 5% of shares to fund for ‘public good’The $48bn giveaway comes amid concerns about the tech and as the company prepares for a stock market listingLauren AlmeidaMon 19 Oct 2026 08.51 EDTFirst published on Mon 19 Oct 2026 06.47 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAnthropic has said it will commit 5% of its shares to a fund for the “public good”, as the AI developer behind the Claude chatbot seeks to bolster its appeal before its stock market listing.The company announced it would commit the shares, worth around $48bn (£36bn) at its latest valuation in May, subject to shareholder approval. It will add a further 2% of its stock to the fund for every 50% increase in its value above an undisclosed baseline.What are self-replicating ‘AI worms’, and why is Anthropic worried about them?Read moreThe fund will allow Anthropic to “explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations”, the company said.The move comes amid growing public nervousness about AI, from the threat to human labour to the impact on the environment and its influence on social behaviours.“AI may generate enormous economic value, but it could also cause instability for many workers,” Anthropic wrote in a blogpost.It said that while it had already committed $200m to addressing the issue, “given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed. The fund will have the versatility to pursue them.”The company, which is preparing to list on the stock market, has called for aslowdownin breakneck development of AI, a warning laterechoed by rivals such as OpenAI.Anthropic was valued at $965bn in May when it raised $65bn in a funding round. The company is reportedly considering a $1.5tn valuation when it floats on the stock market, with an IPO planned for November.Last week, Anthropic said some of its AI models could soon become “self-replicating” and find ways to infiltrate internet-connected devices such as smart fridges and automatic vacuum cleaners.View image in fullscreenElon Musk plans to ‘give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America’.Photograph: Gonzalo Fuentes/ReutersIt said that once this happens, the models would be able to power themselves without the need of datacentres.Elon Musk, the chief executive of Tesla and founder of SpaceX, responded to Anthropic’s plans for a public benefit fund on social media by pledging to give some of his own shares away.“I recommend giving the shares directly to the public,” he wrote. “This is what I will be doing.”He later announced: “Next year, I will give one of mySpaceXshares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many.”Shares in SpaceX, which is listed on the Nasdaq in the US, rose by 1% in pre-market trading on Monday. The company has lost about 9% of its value since it joined the stock market in June.OpenAI, the developer behind ChatGPT, also reportedly engaged in early talks to give a 5% stake in its organisationto the US government.Anthropic, which was founded in 2021 by seven former OpenAI employees, was established as a public benefit corporation. It means that all of the company’s directors must balance financial returns with its public interest mission.Explore more on these topicsAnthropicAI (artificial intelligence)Technology sectorStock marketsIPOsElon MuskSpaceXnewsShareReuse this content

title: France hit by debt sell-off as violent protests unnerve investors | France | The Guardian
description: Difference between French and German borrowing costs widens after public buildings burned and shops looted
Author: Lauren Almeida
Headline: Difference between French and German borrowing costs widens after public buildings burned and shops looted
Content: A town hall in the French city of Limoges was set on fire during the protests.Photograph: SDIS 87/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenA town hall in the French city of Limoges was set on fire during the protests.Photograph: SDIS 87/AFP/Getty ImagesFranceFrance hit by debt sell-off as violent protests unnerve investorsDifference between French and German borrowing costs widens after public buildings burned and shops lootedLauren AlmeidaMon 19 Oct 2026 11.23 EDTFirst published on Mon 19 Oct 2026 03.32 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFrance has been hit by a fresh wave of selling in its bond and stock markets afterviolent protestsover the weekend led to thousands of arrests and left public buildings burned and hundreds of shops looted across the country.10:46France protests escalate with riots, looting and 2,400 arrests - The LatestThe chaos has spooked investors as analysts worried that it would undermine Paris’s efforts to cut spending and reduce its debt.The yield on the government’s 10-year bonds rose by as much as 16 basis points to 4.94% on Monday. Yields rise when prices fall, and the bond market sell-off pushed France’s borrowing costs close to a 24-year high.This widened the difference between the French and German 10-year borrowing costs – which is a metric for the risk premium attached to French debt – towards its highest level in 14 years.Analysts at Goldman Sachs said European sovereign risk was back in focus, with fiscal concerns about France raising the question of whether there could be a repeat of the eurozone debt crisis of 15 years ago.“The risks of disorderly market escalation and real economy contagion look notably lower. But the fundamental fiscal challenges for some countries – especially in France – look harder now than in 2011-15,” the investment bank said.“The issue of how to deal with fundamental sovereign risk remains unresolved in the euro area, requiring credible fiscal consolidation.”The two-year French bond yield rose by nine basis points to 3.64%.Concerns about France’s instability knocked the euro down to a 17-month low against the pound on Monday morning, when sterling rose to €1.188.1:29‘It’s hell’: residents reel after violent weekend riots across France – videoViolence erupted across France after weeks of relatively peaceful demonstrations over conditions in schools and the cost of living, prompting the French president, Emmanuel Macron, to condemn the “unbridled violence” in a televised address on Sunday night.Tens of thousands of people have attended peaceful marches to demand more teachers and repairs to decrepit schools, but different groups have clashed with police in cities including Paris, Bordeaux, Nice and Marseille.Jim Reid of Deutsche Bank said the protests “won’t make it easy for the international community to be totally comfortable buying OATs”, referring to French government bonds.“With France already facing a difficult fiscal backdrop and the 2027 election approaching, the weekend adds another layer of political risk for markets,” he said.The 30-year bond, which is a benchmark for the French government’s long-term cost of borrowing, rose by ten basis points to 5.46%.The rises will put further strain on France’s public finances as the government tries to pass a budget for next yearto rein in its deficit.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionFrance’s debt-to-GDP stood at 115.6% in 2025, while its budget deficit was 5.1%, compared with 94.3% and 4.3% respectively for the UK.The unrest adds to “concerns about the political and fiscal troubles in France”, said Neil Wilson, Saxo UK’s investor strategist.“It underscores how hard it will be for a government to enact the kind of spending restraint required to get the deficit down.”The French government is preparing a budget that would involve cutting pensions spending and funding for government departments, excluding defence. There are growing fears, however, that political pressure could derail the plans, which could push up borrowing further and add more to the country’s debt pile.The euro also slipped against the US dollar, down by 0.4% at one stage on Monday to $1.1197.France’s Cac 40 index, which tracks the biggest companies listed in Paris, fell by 1.4% , compared with a 1.1% drop on the pan-European Stoxx 600 index.French bank stocks were among the fallers, with Société Générale and BNP Paribas down more than 3%.Other European stock markets also weakened, with Italy’s FTSE Mib down 1.6% and Spain’s Ibex dropping by 1.9%.Daniela Hathorn, a senior market analyst at Capital.com, said investors were concerned that higher borrowing costs would increase France’s debt-servicing expenses, reducing its fiscal flexibility at a time when growth is already subdued.“But France is not alone,” he said. “Spain faces its own political constraints around budgets and fiscal reforms, although stronger economic growth provides some protection, while Italy’s substantial debt stock leaves it particularly sensitive to prolonged periods of elevated yields.”Explore more on these topicsFranceBondsStock marketsEuropeProtestEuroCost of living crisisnewsShareReuse this content

title: We must tax the wealth of billionaires, not just income. California can lead the way | Rohit Khanna | The Guardian
description: Will California stand with the working class or the oligarchs in the vote this November?
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Will California stand with the working class or the oligarchs in the vote this November?
Content: ‘For too long, Democrats have answered to corporate donors before workers.’Photograph: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/APView image in fullscreen‘For too long, Democrats have answered to corporate donors before workers.’Photograph: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/APOpinionUS politicsWe must tax the wealth of billionaires, not just income. California can lead the wayRohit KhannaWill California stand with the working class or the oligarchs in the vote this November?Mon 19 Oct 2026 06.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 11.15 EDTShareThe Democratic party has a choice to make. Are we going to be New DealDemocratsor corporate Democrats? Are we standing with the working class or the tech oligarchs?Proposition 40, California’s billionaire tax, is the most important ballot initiative in America and a fight for the soul of our party.Senator Bernie Sanders and I stand with the nurses and healthcare workers who put Prop 40 on the ballot. GovernorGavin Newsomstands with Peter Thiel, Sergey Brin and Elon Musk, Trump backers who all oppose it.Prop 40is a one-time 5% tax on the roughly 250 billionaires who live in the state. Together they hold wealth equal to half of California’s economy. That wealth is up 20% this year alone.Donald Trump doesn’t just love billionaires, he loves multimillionaires tooRead moreIf they paid this tax, they would beworth the same as they were on Labor Day of this year. That’s the speed at which their wealth is growing. The tax would raise about $100bn,90% of itfor healthcare. It would help keep 3 million Californians from losing coverage. Trump’s cuts could cost Medi-Calmore than $30bn a year, and this tax would help fill that gigantic hole.Thiel, Brin and Musk have all funded Trump and his party. Thiel gave$1.25m to elect Trumpin 2016. Brin gavenearly $500,000 to the Republican National Committeelast year. Musk spentroughly $290mto help return Trump to power. On 8 October, Trump awarded Brin and Muskthe National Medal of Science.Brin has spent$102mto kill Prop 40. Thiel gave$3mto block it. Musk attacked it on X,warning that “they will eventually apply the ‘wealth tax’ to everyone”. The day after Trump’s ceremony, Newsomendorsed Prop 42, Brin’s measure to cancel it.Billionaires haveoutspent Prop 40’s supporters more than five to one. Musk has given$366nto federal campaigns in this election cycle alone.Tax billionaires so they can’t buy democracy.I have made my choice. I endorsed Prop 40, and I will vote no on Prop 42. The California Democratic partytook the same positions in August. The governor has made the opposite choice on both.Hefought to keep Prop 40 off the ballot. When the healthcare workers behind itoffered to cut the rate to 2%if he would back it, he said no. Now the No on 40 campaignfeatures him in its ads.Most cynically, Newsom has become the poster child forProp 42, a billionaire-written provision, which would ban California from ever taxing billionaire wealth.He will sadly be more remembered for trying to tank Prop 40 (taxing billionaires) than helping pass Prop 50 (redistricting).Bernie and I believe the fight doesn’t stop with Prop 40. In March, weintroduced the Make Billionaires Pay Their Fair Share Act, a 5% annual tax on America’s 938 billionaires, worth $8.2tn.It would raise more than $4tn over a decade, enough to reverse Trump’s $1.1tn in healthcare cuts, send $12,000 to every family of four making $150,000 or less, and fund free childcare and free college.I am with the working class.In 1911, Wisconsin pioneered the income tax because a property tax on land was no longer enough once industry was producing most of the wealth. Two years later, the country adopted the 16th amendment.Today, California is pioneering a billionaire tax for an economy where explosive asset appreciation escapes ordinary taxation. If voters pass Prop 40, California will be the first place to figure out how to tax billionaire wealth, setting a model for the nation and the world.For too long, our party has answered to corporate donors before workers. The factory towns and rural counties our governing class ignored stopped believing us. Trump promised to fight for them, then cut taxes for billionaires and cut Medicaid. We will not win those voters back by protecting the same billionaires in Sacramento. You cannot oppose the Trump administration while doing the bidding of its donors.Anyone who wants to lead this party has to say where they stand on Prop 40.Every society is taxed. The only question is who will pay. In Trump’s America, working people pay more than they should, while billionaires are so unburdened that they are becoming trillionaires. In the America we seek, billionaires and trillionaires will pay their fair share, while working people will be unburdened.Will California this November stand with the working class or the oligarchs?Rohit Khanna is aUS congressman and attorney serving as the US representative from California’s 17th congressional districtExplore more on these topicsUS politicsOpinionUS income inequalityElon MuskPeter ThielGavin NewsomDemocratscommentShareReuse this content

title: Eagles QB Hurts reportedly played after not sleeping for 36 hours amid blood clot diagnosis | Philadelphia Eagles | The Guardian
description: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will remain sidelined indefinitely with blood clots that have traveled to his lungs
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will remain sidelined indefinitely with blood clots that have traveled to his lungs
Content: Jalen Hurts won Super Bowl LIX with the Eagles.Photograph: Alastair Grant/APView image in fullscreenJalen Hurts won Super Bowl LIX with the Eagles.Photograph: Alastair Grant/APPhiladelphia EaglesEagles QB Hurts reportedly played after not sleeping for 36 hours amid blood clot diagnosis28-year-old set to miss season after diagnosisTanner McKee has taken over as Eagles starterAgenciesMon 19 Oct 2026 14.40 EDTFirst published on Mon 19 Oct 2026 11.13 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GooglePhiladelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is set to miss the rest of the season after further testing ⁠revealedblood clotshad traveled from his leg to his lungs, the team announced on Monday.Hurts’s condition is considered stable and ⁠he “has no significant ⁠functional limitations,” ​the team said. His treatment for a new diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary ⁠emboli will involve blood thinners, during which time he is unable to participate in contact activities.The Rams have managed to transform themselves from a superteam to a midteamRead moreThe 28-year-old’s prognosis is good and the Eagles said they expect ​a full recovery with no long-term ‌effects.Specialists in England ‌initially diagnosed superficial clots in Hurts’s left calf before Philadelphia’s loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on 11 October.According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, he was at the hospital until 4am and was advised by doctors not to sleep as a precautionary measure. That would mean he had not slept for 36 hours when the Eagles kicked off against the Jaguars.Further testing has discovered multiple blood clots in his lungs.“We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners,” the team’s statement concluded. “In the meantime, he ‌will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will ​have no long-term effects.”Hurts hadn’t missed more than two games in a season since becoming the Eagles’ full-time starter in 2021. He has led the Eagles to five straight playoff appearances, three NFC East titles and two Super Bowl appearances, beating the Chiefs 40-22 two years ago.Tanner McKee started for Hurts against the Panthers. McKee finished 26 of 45 for 215 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ 25-14 loss to Carolina. The Eagles (2-4) have lost four consecutive games for the first time since 2020.Hurts has eight touchdown passes and three interceptions with 933 yards passing this season. He is in the middle ofa five-year, $255m extension, including $179.3m guaranteed, that takes him through the 2028 season.The Eagles stunned fans when they drafted Hurts out of Oklahoma in the second round in 2020. They seemingly had Carson Wentz entrenched at QB and had more pressing needs. But Hurts supplanted Wentz and became one of the top quarterbacks in theNFL.Explore more on these topicsPhiladelphia EaglesNFLUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Davies ensures Spurs off the bottom after first win of season against Coventry | Premier League | The Guardian
description: James Maddison scored an excellent first goal, before Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies wrapped up the scoring as Spurs beat a stubborn Coventry 3-1
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: James Maddison scored an excellent first goal, before Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies wrapped up the scoring as Spurs beat a stubborn Coventry 3-1
Content: Ben Davies scored from just outside the area in stoppage time, which made it 3-1 to Spurs.Photograph: Kieran McManus/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenBen Davies scored from just outside the area in stoppage time, which made it 3-1 to Spurs.Photograph: Kieran McManus/ShutterstockPremier LeagueDavies ensures Spurs off the bottom after first win of season against CoventryJacob Steinbergat the Tottenham Hotspur StadiumMon 19 Oct 2026 17.05 EDTLast modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 19.15 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTottenham are level with Beyoncé at last. Progress is represented in Roberto De Zerbi’s side earning only their sixth home win in thePremier Leaguesince November 2024. Cynics will point out that this spectacular stadium has hosted as many Beyoncé gigs during that time, but Spurs are finally singing a happier tune after dragging themselves out of the bottom three thanks to a messy but gritty 3-1 win over Coventry.It was not especially convincing. Coventry raged at the second Spurs goal, delivered when Omar Marmoush responded to Jack Rudoni’s equaliser for the visitors with a vicious effort in the 59th minute. Relief poured out of Marmoush after his first goal since joining on loan from Manchester City, but should it have stood? The Egyptian forward, who otherwise had a quiet game, was fortunate not to be penalised for an elbow on Milan van Ewijk.‘Like a family’: De Zerbi credits players’ talk and bonding trip for improving TottenhamRead moreFrank Lampard looked bewildered. The night belonged to Spurs, who have their first win of the season. James Maddison marked his first start in 536 days by opening the scoring with a brilliant goal. Ben Davies, on as a substitute, calmed the nerves by drilling in the third goal in added time and the home fans were also cheered by Dejan Kulusevski coming on to make his first appearance after more than a season out.The hope for Spurs was that the sight of Kulusevski on the bench would give the crowd an emotional lift. The Swede was back in the squad for the first time since sustaining a knee injury in May 2025 and has been missed. Spurs, who have struggled without Kuluseveki’s creativity, needed to cling to the positivity after their resolute draw at Manchester United.The encouraging thing is that they have been starting games well. This time, though, there were some early jitters after De Zerbi’s switch to a back three. Mohammed Kudus was a surprise choice as an attacking right wing-back, Archie Gray partnered Sandro Tonali in midfield and Coventry had the first chance, a fast break ending with Tatsuhiro Sakamoto watching his deflected shot spin over.View image in fullscreenJack Rudoni beats Antonin Kinsky to give the visitors hope.Photograph: Jonny Weeks/The GuardianThere were a few groans, but Spurs showed rare mental fortitude and struck through another creator rebuilding his career after serious injury. Kudus, lively and direct, provided the spark with a dart past Jay Dasilva. The Ghanaian laid a pass off to Maddison and the No 10, whose every touch had been booed by Coventry supporters apparently still seething with the England international leaving his boyhood club 10 years ago, used his right instep to beat Carl Rushworth with a crisp bending shot from 25 yards.It was a lovely movement for Maddison, who beamed at his first goal since scoring in aEuropa League semi-finalagainst Bodø/Glimt on 1 May 2025. He slogged through his rehab, never giving in, and his enthusiasm was infectious. Even Lampard had to smile when Maddison tracked back to stop a counterattack and apologised after smashing the ball into the Coventry bench.Coventry were slow to respond. Not that Spurs were flowing before half-time. Maddison was involved in some bright moves and Dominic Solanke jabbed a shot over but De Zerbi must have wanted the passing to be sharper. A slick exchange between Sidiki Cherif and Brandon Thomas-Asante was a reminder that this was not over. Thomas-Asante surged past Jan Paul van Hecke and towards Antonin Kinsky, only for Micky van de Ven to intervene with a crucial challenge.Spurs did not heed the warning. A lethargic start to the second half featured Van Hecke ambling out of defence and losing the ball. Coventry countered, Rudoni pushing down the left. The midfielder exchanged passes with Caleb Yirenkyi and Spurs froze. Rudoni shot against Thomas-Asante, retrieved possession, chested the ball down and jabbed it past Kinsky to draw Coventry level.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenJames Maddison curls his shot home for Tottenham’s first goal.Photograph: Dylan Martinez/ReutersStung into action, Spurs raised the intensity and Tonali sent two shots over. Coventry looked uncertain but they raged when the home side regained their lead. Marmoush took a pass, turned and caught Van Ewijk in the face with an elbow. Yet Andrew Madley permitted play to continue with the Coventry right-back on the floor, allowing Marmoush to spin into space and blast an exquisite shot past Rushworth from 20 yards.It was a stunning way for the Egyptian to score for the first time since May. There was no intervention from Paul Tierney, the video assistant referee, and the away end reacted with astonishment when the goal was replayed on the big screens.Coventry were fired by a sense of injustice. They pushed for another equaliser and produced a spell of concerted pressure, only for Spurs to defend their box with determination.De Zerbi sought more energy by bringing on Mateus Fernandes and Conor Gallagher. The Italian took his squad to Marbella for some warm weather training last week. Spurs, who pushed Coventry into 17th place, will hope sunnier times are on the way.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueTottenham HotspurCoventry Citymatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: The Rams have managed to transform themselves from a superteam to a midteam | Los Angeles Rams | The Guardian
description: Los Angeles were tipped as a Super Bowl contender after assembling a star studded lineup. Now they’ve lost three of their last four games
Author: Alex Kirshner
Headline: Los Angeles were tipped as a Super Bowl contender after assembling a star studded lineup. Now they’ve lost three of their last four games
Content: Matthew Stafford walks off the field after Sunday’s loss to the Cardinals.Photograph: Eric Thayer/Los Angeles Times/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMatthew Stafford walks off the field after Sunday’s loss to the Cardinals.Photograph: Eric Thayer/Los Angeles Times/Getty ImagesLos Angeles RamsThe Rams have managed to transform themselves from a superteam to a midteamLos Angeles were tipped as a Super Bowl contender after assembling a star studded lineup. Now they’ve lost three of their last four gamesAlex KirshnerMon 19 Oct 2026 07.11 EDTLast modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 11.14 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Rams were supposed to be the closest thing theNFLhad seen to a superteam in some time. Instead, they’re 2-4, have lost three of their last four games and are last in the NFC West. So much has gone awry, so quickly.Sunday was rock bottom (for now). The Rams lost to the division’s ugly stepchild, the Cardinals – a team they had beaten in 16 of their last 19 meetings – on a day when Arizona didn’t manage to score a touchdown. They didn’t need to, because Arizona kicker Chad Ryland connected on six field goal attempts, the last one a 43-yarder as time expired. The game was a tale of two kickers, in that the Cardinals had a superb one and the Rams didn’t have one at all. Days after releasing Harrison Mevis following a league-worst four misses in the season’s first five weeks, the Rams came into this game with Blake Grupe, whom they’d plucked off the Jets practice squad. Grupe got hurt covering a kickoff return in the first quarter, leaving the Rams literally kickerless for the duration. (Mevis, a big fella whose nickname is the Thick Kicker, or “Thiccer,” has about 80lbs on the 5ft 7in Grupe.)Eagles QB Jalen Hurts to miss rest of season after blood clots travel to his lungsRead moreThe absence of a specialist kicker affected the game. The Rams tried for a two-point conversion after a touchdown in the second quarter, preferring not to have punter Ethan Evans attempt a point after. The Cardinals sacked Matthew Stafford, and the attempt failed. In the third quarter, the Rams faced a fourth-and-one at the Arizona 27-yard line, in what would normally be easy field-goal range. (Of course, Sean McVay may have gone for it anyway in such a spot.) Unable to even consider a kick here, the Rams pushed up the middle and were stacked up at the line for a turnover on downs. Arizona drove the other way for three points.Sean McVay’s bunch could have won anyway. When the Rams tied the game with 42 seconds left, McVaydidsound out his punter, Evans, who nailed his PAT, suggesting maybe he was more reliable as a kicker than his coach believed. But then the Rams’ defense had a meltdown, taking an unnecessary roughness flag and allowing Jacoby Brissett to quickly march Arizona 40 yards to set up Ryland’s winner. Final score: 18-16 to Arizona, an utter disaster for the home team.A bit of everything has gone wrong. Prized defensive end Myles Garrett, the best defensive player in the world, is yet to return as he rehabs from knee surgery. Future Hall of Fame defensive tackle Aaron Donald came out of a years-long retirement and has looked, well, like a man who has come out of a years-long retirement. The Rams had a solid performance against the run in this game but entered it having given up the sixth-most ground yards in football.Meanwhile, Stafford has only looked like his MVP self in one game all year, a Week 2 romp over the very meh Giants. Despite facing less pressure than any other QB in the league,per Sports Reference, Stafford has not been able to make his usual magic. Part of it is that he’s been rushing to get the ball out quickly; his 2.2-second average time to throw ishis quickest rate on record. Puka Nacua has only played in four games, and Davante Adams, who has served as the No 1 wideout in his absence, left Sunday’s game with a suspected knee injury. Things feel like they’re falling apart rapidly for a team expected to compete for the Super Bowl.There is not much good news for the Rams, but there is this: The Chargers moved to 0-6 with a loss to the Chiefs, meaning the Rams still comfortably have the best record of a team based at SoFi Stadium. The two Angeleno clubs face each other in two weeks. That matchup will not be for the faint of heart.MVP of the weekView image in fullscreenCJ Stroud had a successful trip to London.Photograph: Henning Von Jagow/Action Plus/ShutterstockCJ Stroud, quarterback, Houston Texans.The 25-year-old had his best game of the season in a 34-31 shootout win over the Jaguars in London, as Houstonians watched early in the morning. Stroud led a game-winning field goal drive after Jacksonville’s rocket-legged kicker, Cam Little, tied things up late with a 60-yard field goal. The winning drive was a fitting capper for Stroud, who threw an interception but was usually steady, and mixed in more of the sizzle that had come with the steak early in his career. Stroud finished 24-of-34 for 312 yards and three scores and didn’t take a sack. His best work came in tandem with receiver Jaylin Noel, who had a 50-yard catch to set up a critical Houston TD just before half-time. Noel also caught a touchdown. Newly acquired wideout Marvin Harrison Jr caught three of his four targets for 34 yards.Stat of the week45.The previously winless Titans ran that many plays in their 26-20 win over the moribund Colts, who fell to 2-4 and strayed even further from relevance under head coach Shane Steichen and GM Chris Ballard. It’s the fewest plays a winning team has run all season, three behind the 48 the Seahawks had in their season-opening Super Bowl rematch against the Patriots. It’s not as if the Titans did all that much with those offensive snaps, either. Cam Ward needed 22 throws to reach a whopping 102 yards but still outplayed Daniel “Dimes” Jones, who took six sacks and threw two picks. A blocked punt keyed the comeback, and rookie wideout Carnell Tate, the No 4 pick in this year’s draft, caught his first career touchdown. Tennessee had lost a mesmerizing 11 in a row in the division. Poor Jonathan Taylor: the supremely talented running back deserves better than playing on a team like the Colts.Video of the weekAllow content provided by a third party?This article includes content hosted onembed.bsky.app. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as the provider may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content,click 'Allow and continue'.Allow and continueDallas Goedert was just minding his business, running a corner route against the Panthers, whenhisbusiness becameourbusiness. Carolina cornerback Will Lee III struggled to stay with the Eagles veteran and resorted to a particular brand of grabbiness. Lee, exposed by the route Goedert had run, decided to expose the tight end in a different way. A defensive pass interference call gave the Eagles a first down, but it wasn’t enough to save them in what became a 25-14 home loss. The Birds lost their fourth in a row and continue to reel in an NFC East thatsomebodyis going to have to win.Elsewhere around the leagueView image in fullscreenCaleb Williams was on superb form in his return from injury.Photograph: Kevin C Cox/Getty Images-- Caleb Williams looks fine. The Bears’ franchise QB returned from a right hamstring strain that had kept him out since Week 2, and he led Chicago to a 31-23 win over the Falcons. Williams didn’t throw an incomplete pass until his 13th attempt of the game, three minutes into the second quarter, and completed 30 of his 36 throws for 305 yards and a touchdown. It wasn’t entirely peaches and cream, as the four sacks Williams took were his most in a game since a September 2025 loss to the Bears. But in general, he was comfortable with the speed of the game and kept the Bears on track despite a run game that never took off.-- The Steelers are doing it again, and by “it,” I mean “contending in the AFC North despite being deeply unpleasant to watch.” Pittsburgh came back from 13-0 down to beat the woeful Buccaneers in Tampa, 26-19, and move to 4-2. Combined with the Browns’ buzzer-beating win over the Ravens, that result left all three of those teams tied atop the division with the Bengals (on bye) just a half-game behind. Aaron Rodgers looked as athletic as a 58-year-old uncle, taking five sacks and throwing a pick on a screen pass. The Steelers cartoonishly squandered a first-and-goal at the three-yard line after the Bucs’ rookie backup, Jalon Daniels, threw an interception to former Buc Jamel Dean late in the fourth quarter. But after settling for three on that series and allowing Daniels to lead a game-tying drive, Pittsburgh got things under control in overtime.Rodgers also tied Peyton Manningfor third on the all-time passing touchdown list (539). Rodgers won’t catch the two men ahead of him: Drew Brees (571) and Tom Brady (649), but the fact that he got this far is a testament to his skill and longevity. In another blast from the past, Pittsburgh’s Jalen Ramsey had two sacks, including the game-ender in OT. Can I interest anyone in the Steel City in a 10-7 record and a home wildcard defeat?-- One team who areextremelypleasant to watch? The Bills, who moved to 5-1 with a 33-30 win in Las Vegas. Josh Allen didn’t have an overwhelming statistical day but produced one of the more magical moments of his career. On a third-and-8 in the red zone in a one-score game, Allen meandered through traffic in the backfield for a full six secondsbefore casually flicking a backhanded looperover six Raiders (five near him, one in the secondary) and into the waiting arms of Keon Coleman for a touchdown.The video speaks for itself. What a player.Explore more on these topicsLos Angeles RamsNFLUS sportsArizona CardinalsWest CoastfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | La Liga | The Guardian
description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis
Author: Sid Lowe
Headline: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis
Content: Lamine Yamal sits on the advertising board after opening the scoring against Real Betis.Photograph: Marcelo del Pozo/ReutersView image in fullscreenLamine Yamal sits on the advertising board after opening the scoring against Real Betis.Photograph: Marcelo del Pozo/ReutersLa LigaWill that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first testThe 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real BetisSid LoweMon 19 Oct 2026 13.29 EDTLast modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 19.08 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWhen at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day,Real Betisfans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said.At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and healwayshas the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine dothat,whateverthatwas, in Istanbul – an “almostrabona”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,”he wrote.Real Madrid demand La Liga president resign over Goebbels comparisonRead moreTo which Lamine Yamal responded by doing another strange thing that same afternoon, scoring another brilliant goal to setBarcelonaon the way to a 5-2 win over Betis in a game that made history. And if Lamine Yamal had been a little lucky three days before, momentarily losing control only for the rebound to bounce back to him like the ball knew where it would rather be, this was all him and veryhim. The move started with Gerard Martín losing his boot and ended with pretty much everyone else losing their heads. In Martín’s momentary absence, Rodri dropped into defence and began it from there, the ball moved across the box and back until it was played up to Lamine Yamal. His superb pass with the outside of the boot unlocked everything and then, receiving again just inside Betis’s half, he set off.There’s a moment, Lamine Yamal says, when you can sense the anticipation, feel people getting up one after the other all along the stand, a wave accompanying you, moving with you. At that moment, he says, there’s some inner power and you feel like Superman or Spider-Man; the defenders are robots, he says, and however good a robot is, however well programmed to stop him, ahuman is better. Too fast, too agile, too inspired. Too much thought gone into this, too much psychology. Man against the machines,code this. He rolled the ball one way with his left foot, flicked it the other with the heel of his right, and from the edge of the box, sent it flying into the far top corner.View image in fullscreenLamine Yamal tries to get away from Dani Ceballos and Facundo Bernal.Photograph: Antonio Pozo/Pressinphoto/ShutterstockSomehow. Sometimes you have nothing new to say,you know? It’s not big and it’s not clever but sometimes only swearing will do: sometimes onlyholy shit!hits the spot. Sometimes you can be sitting alone on the sofa and still shout:“Oh, my God!”, call them in to watch this. But it won’t be the same when they do, even if it’s sort of better: a chance to slow it down and break it down, see the detail, work out how he did it, like you’re ever going to do that. Because for all the expectation, it’s still a shock seen live, the purest reaction of all.Words?Pah!This weekend, Gabriel Jesus put it best: as the ball passed him, he just held his head in his hands. Lamine Yamal ran to the corner. Fermín López chased, wiping his brow: woah, whatwasthat? Karim Adeyemi went wagging his fingers. On the touchline Flick almost took off his assistant’s hand with the hardest high five. Teammates ran towards him not so much celebrating as laughing, so good it’s funny and even funnier for being repeated, an outrageous goal his catchphrase. Lamine Yamal sat alongside Jules Koundé on the advertising board, arms crossed like it was easy, like “what areyou lotlosing your heads about?” Maybe it is. And there is something in the way he hit it that felt a little like he put it in the top corner because, well, why not?Might as well.Lamine Yamal got up, stood holding the corner flag, looking about:will that do?If this was the first test Barcelona have faced, it hadn’t taken him 10 minutes to score again, and like that. And that’s the thing. Who knows, this might not even have been the best goal of the weekend: there were glorious moments from Arda Guler and Kylian Mbappé in Real Madrid’s win against Sevilla. Javi Rodríguez’s run was wonderful for Celta Vigo against Alavés. And Pablo Martínez’s shot in Málaga’s 2-5 loss to Real Sociedad was ridiculous. It might not have even been the best shot of this game had Gio Lo Celso’s “goal” not been ruled out. And it definitely might not even be the best Lamine Yamal has scored, but this keeps happening. Statement after statement.He didn’t stop there either: there was an absurd pass from which Adeyemi should have scored. A run through three. Another assist. And the moment that got the Betis fans whistling him: when, with López on the ground and Lamine Yamal going over, Facundo Bernal pushed him, he took a run-up and pushed Bernal back, and the defender head-butted him, seeing red. The game hadn’t stopped with his first either; instead, Rodri said afterwards, it had “everything”. Always watch Betis, especially when they’re playing Barcelona: unbeaten in 15 home games, the last time anyone beat them here was Barça too. And it finished 5-3. This time they were only one short.View image in fullscreenBarcelona’s Gabriel Jesus celebrates scoring their third goal with Lamine Yamal.Photograph: Marcelo del Pozo/ReutersBarcelona had dominated the first 25 minutes, the ball theirs alone but Valentín Gómez headed in to make it 1-1 before Rodri made it 2-1. Within two minutes, Lo Celso had smashed in an extraordinary 25-yard shot on the bounce and the turn to make it 2-2, only for it to be ruled out for a handball 14 seconds earlier. All that before half-time. And yet it was summed up better by the 30 seconds that passed between Álvaro Valles making a superb save at one end and Joan García matching it at the other; by the 59 seconds that passed between that and Jesus getting the third. Or the two minutes 59 seconds between that going in and Abdessamad Ezzalzouli making it 3-2. Then the fight that followed it, Lamine Yamal tumbling maybe a touch too hard and Bernal walking.By the time Lamine Yamal did, at last encouraged to rest, Eric García had scored the fourth and it was done. “With this result, we had to make the change,” Flick said; with tensions rising too. Dani Olmo added a neat fifth and it finished. Betis were furious. Asked how it had left him feeling, their manager, Manuel Pellegrini, said: “impotent”. Lo Celso’s goal shouldn’t have been ruled out and Jesus’s should, he said. Ask how he felt, Fran García said “frustrated, angry … and tired”. They had given everything, the ovation as generous as their effort had been. “This is one of the hardest games inLa Liga,” Rodri said, but Barcelona had won again.That’s nine from nine, a new record. Now, a word of advice from Mr Wolf. When it comes to historic starts, Barcelona’s previous record was under Tata Martino, who you may remember but probably don’t. “This is a nice thing but we want to win titles,” Flick said; Martino did not. Betis were the first team Barcelona have played in the top half of the table. The rest currently sit in 19th, 18th, 17th, 16th, 15th 14th, and 11th. Harder games are coming: Paris Saint-Germain next, then Real Madrid. They also have an injury crisis at the back. But no one is playing like them, and certainly not scoring like them. They have scored39league goals, 48 in 11 matches in all competitions.Quick GuideLa Liga resultsShowDeportivo  A Coruña 1-1 Levante, Espanyol 0-1 Atlético, Villarreal 0-0 Elche, Real Betis 2-5 Barcelona, Valencia 0-0 A Bilbao, Osasuna 2-0 Racing Santander, Celta Vigo 2-1 Alavés, Málaga 2-5 Real Sociedad, Real Madrid 4-1 SevillaMonday:Getafe v Rayo VallecanoWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.When Robert Lewandowski, Ferran Torres and Marcus Rashford went in the summer, when they didn’t manage to sign Julián Álvarez, you couldn’t help asking where the goals were going to come from. The answer was everywhere. Thirteen different players have scored. It turns out that they have the best striker in Europe: Raphinha, the man who is just filling in there,has scored more than anyone else. They may also have the best player at 19, the kid who came back a World Cup winner and still wasn’t satisfied.“After the game against Elche at the start of the season, people were saying: ‘He’s not right,’” Lamine Yamal said. “But I was calm at home, thinking: ‘I’ve just won the World Cup, I’ve not had a break, I know my body: bit by bit I’ll get to the point where I explode and start to score. And those same people will suddenly be saying I’m the best.’” In the first two games, against Elche and Athletic Bilbao, Lamine Yamal did little. Since then he has scored or assisted in every match. Nine goals, 10 assists, and most of them brilliant. He went to the international break and scored after 104 seconds at Wembley, 70 in Seville, and320 in Oviedo. Here, on the day they said this time it’s for real, it took him 530, heads in hands, words stuck in throats, and another win on the way.“It was amazing, a match for all the people who love football,” Flick said. “For me Lamine is the best in the world. I’m happy about his performance; this is what I love to see. And when you see the first goal, it’s unbelievable.”Unbelievable. That’ll do.PosTeamPGDPts1Barcelona930272Atletico Madrid911223Real Madrid914214Real Betis92195Real Sociedad90166Sevilla9-2147Alaves93118Celta Vigo93119Deportivo A Coruna911110Osasuna9-81111Athletic Bilbao71912Villarreal90913Espanyol9-1814Rayo Vallecano7-5815Getafe8-6816Racing Santander9-12817Levante8-4718Elche9-6719Valencia9-9620Malaga9-124Explore more on these topicsLa LigaBarcelonaEuropean club footballReal BetisfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: ‘What the war has done to me inside’: Ukraine’s Svitolina announces separation from Monfils | Tennis | The Guardian
description: The World No 6 Elina Svitolina has opened up about the toll of Russia’s war and the breakup of her marriage with Gaël Monfils
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The World No 6 Elina Svitolina has opened up about the toll of Russia’s war and the breakup of her marriage with Gaël Monfils
Content: ‘This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share,’ Elina Svitolina wrote.Photograph: Robert Prange/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreen‘This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share,’ Elina Svitolina wrote.Photograph: Robert Prange/Getty ImagesTennis‘What the war has done to me inside’: Ukraine’s Svitolina announces separation from MonfilsWorld No 6 Svitolina opens up about toll of Russia’s warFrench star Monfils has retired after glittering careerPress AssociationMon 19 Oct 2026 06.24 EDTLast modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 06.52 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe world No 6 Elina Svitolina has announced she has separated from her husband Gaël Monfils.In an emotional Instagram post, the 32-year-old Ukrainian opened up about the mental toll of Russia’s war against her country, describing sleepless nights and self-doubt. Svitolina said she had come to realise she needed to rediscover herself and could no longer do so within her marriage.“This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share,” she wrote. “Everyone knows how much Ukraine means to me. What I have rarely spoken about is what the war has done to me inside. With time, I came to understand that I need to find my way back to myself and that I cannot do that within our marriage.“It is the hardest truth I have ever had to face and the hardest thing I have ever had to tell the person I love. Gaël listened. He has respected what I need with a strength and grace I will never forget.”View image in fullscreenFans recently learned that Gaël Monfils would not be playing in what was supposed to be his final professional tournament, the Paris Masters, which begins later this month.Photograph: Anne-Christine Poujoulat/AFP/Getty ImagesSvitolina – a four-time grand slam semi-finalist – and the French former world No 6 Monfils, 40, were married in 2021 and have a four-year-old daughter, Skai.“Skai will always come first,” Svitolina added. “Our marriage is ending, but our family is not. Please know that there is no one to blame here. There are only two people who loved each other deeply and a story that is changing shape.”Monfils has seemingly brought forward his retirement from the sport, which was expected to come following a farewell outing at the Paris Masters which begins on 31 October. It emerged last week that the Frenchman, who won 13 career titles, is now featured on the InternationalTennisIntegrity Agency’s list of retired players.Explore more on these topicsTennisnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘Money and medals over safety’: Nassar judge warns gymnasts are still being failed | Gymnastics | The Guardian
description: A decade after Larry Nassar’s crimes were first exposed, survivors and advocates have gathered at the World Gymnastics Championships to call for reform to be a priority
Author: Suzanne Wrack
Headline: A decade after Larry Nassar’s crimes were first exposed, survivors and advocates have gathered at the World Gymnastics Championships to call for reform to be a priority
Content: Larry Nassar in court in Michigan in January 2018.Photograph: Rebecca Cook/ReutersView image in fullscreenLarry Nassar in court in Michigan in January 2018.Photograph: Rebecca Cook/ReutersGymnastics‘Money and medals over safety’: Nassar judge warns gymnasts are still being failedLarry Nassar’s sexual abuse crimes came to light 10 years agoSurvivors gather at world championships to call for reformSuzanne Wrackin RotterdamMon 19 Oct 2026 13.22 EDTLast modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 15.45 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe judge who sentenced the former USA Gymnastics team doctorLarry Nassar to up to 175 years in jailin 2018 for the sexual abuse of more than 250 women and girls has condemned the lack of meaningful change in the decade since Nassar’s crimes were exposed.With the WorldGymnasticsChampionships taking place here this week, Judge Rosemarie Aquilina said human rights must be prioritised over the desire for sporting success.“Nassar was 10 years ago and there have been very few changes that are meaningful,” said Aquilina, who insisted on all 169 impact statements being heard in her courtroom after Nasser’s guilty plea.“I’m not looking for little changes that a lot of people get credit for, I want meaningful change, a lot of meaningful changes, and we’re just not there yet, not in sports, not in life, not in the courtroom, not in the classroom or in the legislature.“I have to ask why? It’s the same answer: it’s money, medals and notoriety over the safety of children and safety is a human right.”Aquilina joined activists, survivors and advocates from Gymnasts for Change International (G4CI) in Rotterdam, who gathered to question why the level of change has been inadequate and what can be done.View image in fullscreen(Left to right): gymnasts Simone Biles, McKayla Maroney, Aly Raisman and Maggie Nichols at a senate hearing about the Larry Nassar case in 2021.Photograph: Saul Loeb/APClaire Heafford, a survivor of abuse within the sport and the chief executive of G4CI, said: “We’re still in a place where survivors aren’t being listened to and where the scale of the reform hasn’t met the scale of the revelations.”Heafford puts the unwillingness to engage with systemic change post-Nassar as “institutional fear, blinkeredness, and the fact that people who work in sport are not very creative”.She said: “It’s incredibly difficult for anybody in the system who wants to create change to do so if there’s resistance above them. It’s incredibly difficult for people in the system to feel empowered as change makers when you’re in such fixed hierarchies.”Gymnastics’ ongoing reckoning: inside fight for survivor-led reform 10 years on from Nasser caseThe event was timed to reflect an opportunity for genuine change as World Gymnastics appoints a new secretary general with Nicolas Buompane stepping down at the end of the year.Minky Worden, of Human Rights Watch, said the reckoning sport faced since Nassar took the wrong form. “On the one hand, you can measure progress in athlete voice and advocacy, in some whistleblower protections, in safeguarding rules across sport – though the rules are there, but the implementation is not,” she said.“Then, on the other hand, you can measure it in the impact gymnastics had in all other sports. I’ve interviewed hundreds of survivors in about 50 sports, winter and summer. Ten years on, just the scale and the severity and the duration of the abuses by the so-called Olympic doctor Larry Nassar caused a reckoning across sport. But the reckoning often took the wrong shape, it took the shape of defence.View image in fullscreenJudge Rosemarie Aquilina addresses Larry Nassar in January 2018.Photograph: Brendan McDermid/Reuters“Except, this is not a small problem, it is a severe problem and any fair assessment would have to say that sport, broadly speaking, including gymnastics, retains the exceptionalism the Catholic church and schools once had.“There was a time when it was really hard to get rid of the abusive priest or teacher because they were moved around to different jurisdictions and continued abusing. That is why the scale and the duration of those abuse catastrophes was so great. Sports still has the same problem.”The former elite acrobatic gymnast Eloise Jotischky, who became the first person towin a civil case against British Gymnasticsfor the abuse she experienced between 2016 and 2018, which included inappropriate weight management techniques and verbal abuse, said there have been some changes, but the issue is with implementation.“There’s still a lot to be done. For example, British Gymnastics have come out with a number of policies, they’ve got their hydration policies, they’ve got their weight management policies. That’s brilliant, but let’s implement them. It’s the implementation that matters because if you don’t implement them and if you’re not monitoring them then what’s the point?”Kim Shore, of Gymnasts for Change Canada, who is a survivor of abuse within the sport and an independent safe sport advocate, wants World Gymnastics to adopt and implement huge cultural reforms if things are to improve. “There’s a crisis of abuse across sport in Canada and yet we’ve seen really no reform and I would say that same lack of action, that same apathy is happening at World Gymnastics,” she said.“Sure, they’ve taken some steps, but they could post new rules anywhere that say: ‘No more weighing of gymnasts. No more gymnasts returning to competition without a doctor’s note. No more coaches moving from one country to another country, if you’re banned in the US, you can’t just take a gymnast from Mexico to the Olympics.’“They could have a whole list of rules and regulations, even if they don’t have any sort of legislative jurisdiction in an area, that’s still going to influence the culture because as soon as the leading body says we’re not weighing gymnasts any more, then when the weighing gets done those coaches know they’re breaking the rules.“If World Gymnastics would come out with a whole list of cultural reforms and started to normalise those within the national federations and then give them backing so that the national federations can go to the clubs all the way down to grassroots, I think we would see faster reform and less resistance.”World Gymnastics, USA Gymnastics, Gymnastics Canada and British Gymnastics have been contacted for comment.Explore more on these topicsGymnasticsUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Cristiano Ronaldo receives 30-day suspension and £215 fine over Portugal walkout | Cristiano Ronaldo | The Guardian
description: The Portuguese FA’s disciplinary council has upheld the charge against the 41-year-old, though the federation’s president has left the door open for a return
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The Portuguese FA’s disciplinary council has upheld the charge against the 41-year-old, though the federation’s president has left the door open for a return
Content: It is unclear whether time already served under a provisional suspension will count towards Cristiano Ronaldo’s 30-day sanction.Photograph: Zed Jameson/PAView image in fullscreenIt is unclear whether time already served under a provisional suspension will count towards Cristiano Ronaldo’s 30-day sanction.Photograph: Zed Jameson/PACristiano RonaldoCristiano Ronaldo receives 30-day suspension and £215 fine over Portugal walkoutDisciplinary council upholds charge against 41-year-oldFifa suspends Egypt’s Hossam Hassan and Mostafa ZikoReutersMon 19 Oct 2026 16.34 EDTFirst published on Mon 19 Oct 2026 14.07 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCristiano Ronaldo has been suspended for 30 days by the Portuguese ⁠FA after leaving the national team camp following a rift with the coach, ⁠Jorge Jesus, over ⁠his role in the side. The federation’s disciplinary council saidit had upheld the chargeagainst ⁠the 41-year-old forward in full and imposed a fine of €255 (£215).Ronaldoleft Portugal’s base in ⁠Copenhagenbefore their Nations League match against Denmark this month,having accused ‌Jesus of twice ‌breaking his wordabout his role after he was an ‌unused substitute against Norway. Jesus denied making any agreement with Ronaldo but left the door open for his return after Portugal’s 2-1 win.Ronaldo’s break with Portugal is sad, fitting, and long overdue | Jonathan WilsonRead moreThe disciplinary council’s non-professional section found Ronaldo had intentionally committed an offence under Article 160(1) ‌of the federation’s disciplinary regulations. Proceedings were opened on 9 October over facts reported two days earlier.The statement did not specify which matches or activities the suspension would cover, or whether time already served under a provisional suspension would count towards the 30-day sanction.Ronaldo later ⁠apologised for failing to acknowledge supporters after the Norway match and for leaving his teammates, saying he remained available for selection after serving any ‌punishment arising from the incident.The Portuguese FA president, Pedro Proença, has said everyone within the federation wanted Ronaldo to return to the national team once the matter was resolved.Meanwhile, Fifa has suspended the Egypt coach, Hossam Hassan, and the forward Mostafa Ziko for ⁠three and five matches respectively, the Egyptian Football Association said on Monday, after they ⁠criticised the referee ⁠following their​3-2 defeat by Argentinain the World Cup.The 60-year-old Hassan was sanctioned after blaming ⁠refereeing errors for his country’s elimination from the tournament in the last 16, while Ziko insulted the ⁠referee in a post-match interview.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIbrahim Hassan, Hossam’s twin and ​Egypt’s national team director, ‌has also been suspended ‌for three matches.“The decisions include the suspension of Hossam Hassan ‌and Ibrahim Hassan for three matches each, while Ziko has been suspended for five matches,” the EFA said in a statement.Explore more on these topicsCristiano RonaldoPortugalnewsShareReuse this content

title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Florian Wirtz takes on more responsibility in Liverpool’s attack while Pierre Sage is under pressure at Crystal Palace
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Florian Wirtz takes on more responsibility in Liverpool’s attack while Pierre Sage is under pressure at Crystal Palace
Content: Josh King; Florian Wirtz; Sven Botman challenging Nicolas Jackson.Composite: Guardian Pictures (via Getty / REX)View image in fullscreenJosh King; Florian Wirtz; Sven Botman challenging Nicolas Jackson.Composite: Guardian Pictures (via Getty / REX)Premier LeaguePremier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s actionFlorian Wirtz takes on more responsibility in Liverpool’s attack while Pierre Sage is under pressure at Crystal PalaceGuardian sportMon 19 Oct 2026 03.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 11.05 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google1In-form Calvert-Lewin causes a ‘ruckus’Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s physicality overpowering Bryan Mbeumo in Manchester United’s area at a corner grabbed him a fifth goal in 10 outings for Leeds: a pretty respectable ratio. “I just tried to cause a ruckus,” said Leeds’ No 9. “I make it difficult for the defender. I read the flight of the ball and was quickest to react. I feel really comfortable [here]. I feel the support from the club and the fans and it is a great feeling stepping on to the pitch, particularly at Elland Road.” Of the contenders to be understudy to Harry Kane as England’s centre-forward, Calvert-Lewin may be the lead act – if he can stay injury-free, which has been a difficulty throughout his career.Jamie JacksonMatch report:Leeds 1-1 Manchester United2Baleba adds fresh energy to UnitedAfter thedefeat to Atlético Madridlast Tuesday, Manchester United’s director of football, Jason Wilcox, could at least sit a bit more comfortably watching Michael Carrick’s side battle to a draw at Elland Road. Lisandro Martínez bemoaned, among other things, the lack of squad depth at United in his post-match comments in Madrid, but one area Wilcox did strengthen over the summer was United’s midfield. Carlos Baleba, a £65m arrival from Brighton, started his first game for the club alongside Andrey Santos, a £50m signing from Chelsea, and the pair held their own against Leeds’ combative midfield three. “They’re both young players adapting to life at this football club and I thought both of them were terrific today,” Carrick said. “That’s a massive positive for us.” As for Martínez, he was taken off at half-time with a tight thigh.Billy MundayView image in fullscreenCarlos Baleba made his mark for Manchester United in midfield.Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images3Wirtz grows into role of Liverpool creatorFlorian Wirtz created nine chances during Liverpool’s comeback win againstBrentford. The German’s effectiveness grew when Brentford were reduced to 10 men but it was still one of Wirtz’s better games in a Liverpool shirt. The playmaker took on responsibility in the second half. Andoni Iraola was happy and perhaps sees a connection growing between Wirtz and Víctor Muñoz. Both of Wirtz’s assists in the league this season have been for Muñoz, a £34.5m summer signing from Osasuna who hugs the touchline and stretches the play with speed and directness. Iraola plays positive, vertical football. Wirtz could be more dangerous if his passes are hitting speedy wingers such as Muñoz and Bradley Barcola.Jacob SteinbergMatch report:Brentford 1-2 Liverpool4Bouaddi belies his years in assured displayAyyoub Bouaddi made his first league start for Manchester City in the win against Ipswich but anyone watching would have thought he was an old hand. Theteenager belied his yearswith a mature performance at the base of midfield, controlling the tempo while keeping things simple in possession and spotting danger when required. The Moroccan cost £85m in the summer from Lille to battle for a place in Enzo Maresca’s revamped side, fighting Enzo Fernández and Elliot Anderson for a spot in the team – and he is looking their equal. “Not bad, yeah?” Maresca joked about Bouaddi’s performance. “I think that the manager is always looking to find minutes and space for good players. Ayyoub is very good. He is very young, coming from France, so we need to help him, not put him under pressure every game. I think he is doing well.”Will UnwinMatch report:Manchester City 3-2 IpswichView image in fullscreenAyyoub Bouaddi has made a promising start in England.Photograph: Ryan Jenkinson/EPA5Arbeloa claims ‘sky is the limit’ for KingIf you were at Craven Cottage on Saturday and didn’t know which three players Álvaro Arbeloa had brought with him from the Real Madrid setup, you would have assumed one of them was Josh King. The 19-year-old has started every league game this season ahead of Emile Smith Rowe in the No 10 position and has already taken on the role of chief creator. King has been in Fulham’s academy since under-nine level and became a regular in the first team under Marco Silva last season. Arbeloa has spoken of wanting to help the youngster raise his level, to help him kick on. “He’s a top talent,” said Arbeloa after King’s all-action performance against Hull that helpedFulhamto their first league win of the campaign. “The sky is his limit. He has the talent, the mentality, the character – he has everything to become a top, top player.”BMMatch report:Fulham 1-0 Hull City6Moyes aggrieved after Rogers escapes redDavid Moyes claimed Chelsea got the rub of the green with the two goals that condemnedEvertonto a first defeat of the season but there was no question it was deserved on the basis of their respective second-half performances. Everton’s response to Pedro Neto’s opener was nonexistent, with Moyes’s decision to introduce a seemingly unfit Christian Nørgaard instead of Hayden Hackney a contributory factor, but they could feel aggrieved about Morgan Rogers avoiding a second yellow card in the 44th minute for leaping into James Garner. With Harrison Armstrong booked for what the referee, Paul Tierney, deemed a reckless challenge on Josh Acheampong earlier in the game, his inconsistency on the Chelsea forward’s tackle was a key moment. “I would love to speak on the referees but I would probably get fined,” said Garner. “All this camera stuff on their heads, you need to keep out of the game. Just let referees ref it and stop making it about them. That’s all I’ve got to say.”Andy HunterMatch report:Everton 0-2 ChelseaView image in fullscreenMorgan Rogers (centre) was not the most popular man on Merseyside at the weekend.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA7Time for Jaissle to switch up defence?Sven Botman was extremely fortunate not to be sent off for a nasty tackle on Nicolas Jackson as Newcastle lost 1-0 at home to Aston Villa, with the excellent Johan Manzambi heading the first-half winner. The rash, high way Botman lunged in on Jackson seemed emblematic of the centre-back’s decline since he suffered a serious knee injury three years ago. The moment has surely arrived for the now under pressure Matthias Jaissle to drop Botman and recall not merely Dan Burn but Fabian Schär, too, in a switch to a more stabilising back three. Newcastle’s failure to keep a clean sheet in their last 13Premier Leaguegames at home – a run stretching back into last season under Eddie Howe – emphasises the need for defensive fortification.
