Moreover Schär’s ball-playing ability, and particularly his dangerous long diagonal passes, would enhance Newcastle’s pretty dismal threat as an attacking force. Tellingly, Jaissle’s team registered only one shot on target on Saturday, paving the way for Unai Emery’s 100th Premier League win as a manager.Louise TaylorMatch report:Newcastle 0-1 Aston Villa8Madueke upstages struggling EzeWhen Arsenal signed Eberechi Eze, it was hard not to be a little suspicious. Though he started his top-level career relatively late, it is rare a player steps up levels at 27 – all the more so given Mikel Arteta is not exactly in love with mavericks and risk. Ultimately, Eze looks better suited to being the main man in a mid-ranking team rather than a cog in a top one which prioritises shape and system above all else. He was anonymous against Nottingham Forest prior to his removal at half-time. ThoughArsenal did not explode thereafter, Noni Madueke did offer greater threat, his speed challenging defenders inside and out before scoring a winning goal that, though fortuitous, also reflected the difference he made. There is surely little chance Eze is picked to start Arsenal’s next game, at Bayern Munich, and he is running out of time to establish himself at the club.Daniel HarrisMatch report:Nottingham Forest 0-1 ArsenalView image in fullscreenEberechi Eze (right) made little impact against Nottingham Forest.Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images9Sage on thin ice after grim trip to seasidePierre Sage is treading on very thin ice atCrystal Palaceafter another disastrous defensive display allowed Brighton to equal their biggest win against their arch rivals. A poor start to the season has been marked by Palace conceding 17 goals in seven league matches – the worst in the division. The chair, Steve Parish, admitted during the international break that the Frenchman’s position remains on “high alert” and, judging by the angry reaction of some Palace fans to the 5-0 thrashing at the Amex Stadium, Sage could be in big trouble. But there must be some sympathy given the failure to adequately replace the influential Maxence Lacroix in central defence after he was sold to Chelsea. That is believed to have led to disagreements with Parish, who has shown a tendency to act quickly if things aren’t going his way. It could be a nerve-racking few days for Sage before Thursday’s trip to face Besiktas in the Europa League.Ed AaronsMatch report:Brighton 5-0 Crystal Palace10Sunderland’s squad buckles under strainSunderland’s problems are stacking up. Brian Brobbey’s continued absence with an injury sustained while playing for the Netherlands is beyond Régis Le Bris’ control but defeat at Bournemouth was self-inflicted. The swift journey from the Championship to the Europa League has become a stumble. Kevin Danso’s red card was by no means the only error committed during a performance where cross words were exchanged between befuddled defenders. Granit Xhaka found himself incapable of exerting anything like the influence he showed last season. Instead, Tyler Adams and Lewis Cook dominated midfield. Trips to Poznan, Milan and Anderlecht await for Sunderland but Le Bris’ squad is struggling to straddle two fronts. A horrible performance at the Vitality Stadium came despite five purported first-team players being restedagainst Torreense. Play like they did on Sunday and a struggle in the bottom half surely awaits. Just about everything that went right last season has taken a turn for the worse.John BrewinMatch report:Bournemouth 2-0 SunderlandPosTeamPGDPts1Man City712212Arsenal76183Brighton718164Chelsea74135Liverpool71126Brentford75107Leeds73108Everton71109Hull71910Ipswich7-4911Newcastle7-4812Aston Villa7-4813Man Utd70714Crystal Palace7-8715AFC Bournemouth7-4616Coventry6-6617Fulham7-3518Nottm Forest7-4519Sunderland7-8420Tottenham Hotspur6-63Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueManchester CityArsenalBrighton & Hove AlbionChelseaLiverpoolBrentfordfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Kawhi Leonard: a hero’s complicated return to the Toronto Raptors | Toronto Raptors | The Guardian
description: The reunion between one of the best players of his generation and the team he helped make an NBA champion is an opportunity to change narratives
Author: Oren Weisfeld
Headline: The reunion between one of the best players of his generation and the team he helped make an NBA champion is an opportunity to change narratives
Content: Kawhi Leonard is back for a second spell with the Raptors.Photograph: Cole Burston/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenKawhi Leonard is back for a second spell with the Raptors.Photograph: Cole Burston/Getty ImagesToronto RaptorsKawhi Leonard: a hero’s complicated return to the Toronto RaptorsThe reunion between one of the best players of his generation and the team he helped make an NBA champion is an opportunity to change narrativesOren WeisfeldMon 19 Oct 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 05.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWhen Kawhi Leonard became a Toronto Raptor for the first time in the summer of 2018, he looked shellshocked. “There’s just more questions you have to ask me in order for me to tell you about myself,” he said, introducing himself to an organization and city he reportedly had no interest in joining.Leonard had fallen out with his former team, the San Antonio Spurs – one of the most respected franchises in professional sports – due todifferences in opinionabout an injury that had limited him to just nine games in the 2017-18 season. The Los Angeles native had hoped to end up in southern California, but instead the Raptors risked it all by swapping franchise cornerstone DeMar DeRozan for one year of an injured, malcontent Leonard. It worked: Leonardled the Raptors to their maiden championshipon the back of a historic playoff run, averaging 30.5 points, 9.1 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.7 steals en route. Leonard won his second finals MVP to go alongside the one he had claimed with the Spurs when he helped them to the title in 2014.LeBron James is everything Philadelphia wants. And everything it can’t stand | Bryan Armen GrahamRead more“The narrative of not wanting to come to this city is gone,” the team’s president, Masai Ujiri, said at that 2018 press conference, speaking to insecure Raptors fans who had watched American players like Vince Carter, Tracy McGrady, and Chris Bosh leave Toronto since the franchise opened its doors in 1995. “We should move past that. Believe in this city. Believe in yourselves … We are proud of who we are.”But even a historic season wasn’t enough to convince Leonard to stay north of the border. After a long and contentious free-agency period managed by his uncle, Dennis Robertson, Leonard spurned the reigning champions in favor of his hometownLos Angeles Clippers. “There wasn’t as much anger in 2019 as there was with Vince Carter or some of the other guys who left,” says Bruce Arthur, who has covered Leonard since 2018 for the Toronto Star. “I think he was given a little bit of special dispensation because he was going home, because he had delivered a title, and because I never felt like there was ever a connection outside of Kawhi the basketball player, with Toronto.”Raptors fans’ anger was instead directed towards the Clippers, who not only showed up to almost every Raptors game during the championship season, but who also, we now know, wentunder the table to ensure Leonardsigned lucrative endorsement deals totaling over $50m – violating the NBA’s salary cap rules.Robertson was suspended for five years and Clippers owner Steve Ballmer was handed the harshest punishment in NBA history, including the loss of five first-round draft picks and a year-long suspension. However, thanks to a side-deal between the NBA and its Players Associationexecuted to avoid arbitration, Leonard was given a relatively light $700,000 fine (he has earned $375m in salaryso far in his career).“Kawhi’s … gotten away really clean from what is obviously out-of-bounds behavior,” says Arthur, whoreportedthat Leonard – as much as hepleads ignoranceto all this – was in the room when Robertson asked the Raptors for an ownership stake in the Toronto Maple Leafs and at least $10m per year in no-show sponsorship deals in 2019. “So, perfect heist-type stuff from Kawhi.”Despite being one of the greatest players of his generation, the 35-year-old has burned bridges on his way out of every franchise he’s played for. Spurs fans are still upset by the way his injury was handled in 2017-18, while Clippers fans are distraught about being left holding the bag without even a genuineapology from Leonard.But Raptors fans have much more complicated feelings towards the seven-time All-Star – arguably the best player in franchise history.On the one hand, “There was a sense of defiance, especially the first year after Kawhi left [when the Raptors lost to the Boston Celtics in Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semi-finals] ...and there was a great deal of pride that went into that,” says William Lou, the host and creator of the Hello and Welcomepodcast.But as time went on, “The Clippers were humbled in a basketball sense. They never could get that version of Kawhi … that Toronto got in their one year, and so it’s hard to be too mad.”View image in fullscreenKawhi Leonard celebrates the Raptors’ title in 2019.Photograph: Nathaniel S Butler/NBAE/Getty ImagesArthur says Raptors fans will always associate Leonard with the championship win. “I think the bottom line isn’t necessarily about a lack of moral reckoning by Raptors fans as much as: this guy’s so good that you forgive him, right?” says Arthur. “The [championship] was the greatest moment in franchise history by galaxies. Two and a half million people on the streets of Toronto for the parade. That was one of the best days Toronto’s ever had.”The sentiment was seemingly shared by the organization. Despite being frustrated by the way his previous free agency unfolded, the Raptors front office couldn’t pass up the opportunity to grab the lifeline Leonard represented – even in his mid 30s. The Raptors have failed to win a playoff series since 2020, a stretch that includes three grim seasons of 30 wins or fewer. Last season, the franchise pulled itself out of the dregs of the league thanks to a star leap from 25-year-old Scottie Barnes and a handful of smart trades and draft picks, but the Raptors looked like a relatively expensive, middle-of-the-pack team with a difficult path towards contention until Leonard not only became available, but pushed his way towards Toronto.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“This city took a liking to my family, and I took a liking to this city,” Leonard said in the team-owned documentary seriesOpen Gymafter the Raptors traded Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two first-round picks, two second-round picks and a pick-swap for him in mid-September. “Hopefully they embrace me back and [I] give them my all again, and we can make something special happen once again.”Although there were extenuating circumstances leading to Leonard’s return – he and the Clippers areunder investigationby the Justice Department – it is meaningful that he chose the Raptors over big-market championship contenders like Miami, Minnesota, and Detroit. It’s also important that he proclaimed his desireto retire a Raptor beforesigning a two-year, $115m extension with the franchise. “He deserves to have his jersey retired somewhere,” says Lou. “But due to the circumstances of his career, he kind of was a player without a home.”Leonard now has a chance to rewrite his complicated legacy with a familiar franchise. Leading the Raptors back to anywhere near the promised land would ensure him a jersey retirement ceremony, a first-ballot Hall of Fame induction, and Canadian sports immortality.The Raptors, meanwhile, aren’t just getting an upgrade at the wing position; they are getting an all-time great coming off one of the best seasons of his career – an American superstar who experienced all the small cultural discomforts of playing in Toronto and still had such positive memories of the fans, organization, and city that he chose to return to.“It’s a little surreal having this guy who leaves after a championship, and you think the story’s done there, and then he becomes the biggest scandal in theNBA, and then somehow forces his way to the Raptors,” says diehard Raptors fan Imman Adan. “But I definitely think him coming back cements Toronto’s legacy.”It’s complicated, of course. It always will be so long as the Raptors are the lone NBA franchise outside of the United States. But no matter how Leonard’s second tenure in Toronto plays out, his return is a stamp of approval – one that many Raptors fans have been waiting for since the franchise began.Explore more on these topicsToronto RaptorsNBABasketballLos Angeles ClippersUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Brighton & Hove Albion | The Guardian
description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team
Author: Jonathan Wilson
Headline: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team
Content: Brighton are third in the table after a successful start to the season.Composite: Guardian Pictures (via Getty / REX)View image in fullscreenBrighton are third in the table after a successful start to the season.Composite: Guardian Pictures (via Getty / REX)Soccer with Jonathan WilsonBrighton & Hove AlbionBrighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League placeDiego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast teamSign up for our free newsletter hereJonathan WilsonMon 19 Oct 2026 10.51 EDTLast modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 10.52 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFor two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes.This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches ofPremier Leagueregulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League?Brentford began the weekend in third and with, perhaps, a slight sense of frustration that they had drawn four games. Again, they will feel they might have done rather better on Saturday; they were leading Liverpool 1-0 when Yehor Yarmolyuk foolishly flicked his head towards Jérémy Jacquet and was sent off just before half-time.The result was a 2-1 defeatand a sense of an opportunity missed. Bournemouth have not had the easiest start under Marco Rose, butSunday’s 2-0 winover Sunderland perhaps hints at a brighter future.Which left Brighton to carry the charge of the B clubs, which they did in emphatic style, ending a run of four derbies without successwith a crushing 5-0 win. Crystal Palace had been extremely fortunate to survive a first-half battering from Nottingham Forest last week. They were thoroughly outplayed in the early stages again, and this time found themselves 3-0 down inside 10 minutes. Perhaps the opening goal, a cross headed into his own net by Jaydee Canvot, was fortunate, but it was an error induced by the intensity of Brighton’s start. The second goal, a perfectly weighted drive from just inside the Palace half from Diego Gómez, spoke of a side playing with immense confidence. Already this season, 11 different players have scored for Brighton in the league. They have become the image of a side without stars, the whole far greater than the individuals who comprise it.The difference from February, when Brighton last played Palace, is stark. They lost that game 1-0, meaning they had won just one of their previous 12 Premier League games. Generalised grumbling had begun to curdle into calls for Fabian Hürzeler to be sacked. When they lost Carlos Baleba, Jan Paul van Hecke, Danny Welbeck and James Milner over the summer, there were reasons to wonder whether they could keep going with the process of continuous renewal.There were the usual assorted signings, the usual mix of Premier League experience and exotic unknowns. The 19-year-old centre-back Luka Vušković, who spent last season on loan at Hamburg from Tottenham, already looks at home (and who really thought, when Spurs and Brighton effectively swapped centre-backs, with Van Hecke moving to London, that Brighton would not end up with the better of the deal?). The 21-year-old Spanish midfielder Chema Andrés, who arrived from Stuttgart, sparkled from the bench against Arsenal and has excelled in the two games since.But the stand-out performer this season has been a far more familiar name: Pascal Gross, who returned in January after a season and a half at Borussia Dortmund. No player in the Premier League has registered more than his four assists this season. Nobody has run further. He has three goals. He averages a league-high 3.0 key passes a game. To bring back a player who is now 35 has been a masterstroke.The victory over Arsenal before the international break suggested a team capable not merely of accumulating points against the league’s lesser lights, or even of challenging the elite, but of overwhelming them. Arsenal were suffocated by the Brighton press and, while a couple of low-xG long-range finishes in the first half helped, the fact is that Brighton dominated the match to a remarkable extent.The question is whether they can keep it going. Just as their transfer policy is now an accepted feature of the Premier League, so too is Brighton’s mid-season slump. They haven’t won a game in December since 2023. Is this squad strong enough to sustain the challenge? Europe seems not to be unsettling Brighton as it did on their first foray, or as it appears to be draining Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Sunderland – which may be a reflection on the relative quality of the Conference League.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThey are doing this without Kaoru Mitoma, Yankuba Minteh and Mats Wieffer, all of whom should be back at some point over the next month. That suggests the depth of this Brighton squad. It’s always a major step for a club unfamiliar with the Champions League to haul themselves into the top five. At times it often feels a mental barrier as much as anything.But if any of those B clubs are ever going to break into the Champions League, they may never have a better opportunity than Brighton do this season.Explore more on these topicsBrighton & Hove AlbionSoccer with Jonathan WilsonPremier LeaguefeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Crystal Palace to give Sage more time but manager under serious scrutiny | Crystal Palace | The Guardian
description: Pierre Sage is under severe pressure after Crystal Palace’s thrashing at Brighton, with Kieran McKenna and Thomas Frank among the potential candidates to replace him
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Pierre Sage is under severe pressure after Crystal Palace’s thrashing at Brighton, with Kieran McKenna and Thomas Frank among the potential candidates to replace him
Content: Pierre Sage frets on the sidelines during Crystal Palace’s 5-0 defeat against Brighton.Photograph: Gareth Fuller/PAView image in fullscreenPierre Sage frets on the sidelines during Crystal Palace’s 5-0 defeat against Brighton.Photograph: Gareth Fuller/PACrystal PalaceCrystal Palace to give Sage more time but manager under serious scrutinyFrenchman under pressure after Brighton thrashingMcKenna and Frank among potential replacementsEd AaronsMon 19 Oct 2026 11.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 13.53 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GooglePierre Sage has been granted more time to fix Crystal Palace’s defensive issues but he has been warned that things must improve quickly afterthe 5-0 defeat at Brightonon Sunday.The Frenchman’s future was in serious doubt after his side conceded three times inside the opening 10 minutes before equalling the 70‑year record for the club’s heaviest defeat against their arch-rivals. The thrashing means Palace have conceded the most goals in the Premier League: 17 from seven games.Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s actionRead moreThe club chair, Steve Parish, is understood not to have been fully convinced by Sage sincethe 47‑year‑old was appointedto replace Oliver Glasner in the summer. Parish is believed to have considered parting company with Sage on Sunday after 10 matches but decided against a change given that Palace are 14th and not in immediate danger.Sage is expected to remain in charge not only for the Europa League game at Besiktas on Thursday but also the Premier League match against Newcastle on Sunday. But it has been made clear to the former Lens manager that his position is under heavy scrutiny. Kieran McKenna, who Parish approached while the Northern Irishman was at Ipswich, and Thomas Frank will be among the contenders if Sage is sacked.Tensions between Sage and Parish date to the summer transfer window whenPalace failed to secure the manager’s main targets to replace Maxence Lacroixin central defence. Two loanees, Axel Disasi and the teenager Honest Ahanor –, were signed instead from Chelsea and Atalanta respectively. Palace alsomissed out on Malick Fofana to Sunderland on deadline daydespite Sage making the Belgium forward, whom he coached in Lyon’s youth teams, a priority. Palace instead signed Darío Osorio on an initial loan and the Chile forward has played only a handful of minutes.Parish was unhappy with Sage’s treatment of Jaydee Canvot after the France Under-21 international was dropped from the squad forthe home defeat by Ipswich last month. He is also understood to have been angered by Adam Wharton being substituted in that match after Disasi was shown a red card in the first half.Some behind the scenes at Palace have been pushing for Sage to be sacked, but Parish is thought to recognise the headache caused by Disasi’s three-match suspension and injuries to Chadi Riad and Takehiro Tomiyasu and would prefer to give him an opportunity to turn things around.Chris Richards has apologised to Palace supporters after failing to acknowledge them after the Brighton game. “I want to apologise for walking off after the game,” the USA defender wrote on Instagram.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“I was emotional and embarrassed with the result – I know how much this club means to all of you. We have to take responsibility, do better and show that on the pitch.”Explore more on these topicsCrystal PalacenewsShareReuse this content

title: Uefa demands Fifa releases documents relating to World Cup sell-off scheme | Fifa | The Guardian
description: The European governing body has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key material in a letter which also addresses other controversies including the Folarian Balogun affair, peace prize and relations with Donald Trump
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: The European governing body has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key material in a letter which also addresses other controversies including the Folarian Balogun affair, peace prize and relations with Donald Trump
Content: The letter sent by Uefa claims Gianni Infantino’s responses at last week’s meeting of the Fifa council ‘have not begun satisfactorily to address a number of fundamental questions’.Photograph: Kacper Pempel/ReutersView image in fullscreenThe letter sent by Uefa claims Gianni Infantino’s responses at last week’s meeting of the Fifa council ‘have not begun satisfactorily to address a number of fundamental questions’.Photograph: Kacper Pempel/ReutersFifaUefa demands Fifa releases documents relating to World Cup sell-off schemeEuropean governing body gives two-week deadlineLetter addresses other issues including Balogun affairMatt HughesMon 19 Oct 2026 14.52 EDTLast modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 16.06 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleUefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’sWorld Cup sell-off planand other governance issues inits latest critique of football’s world governing body.A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights,the Folarin Balogun affair,the peace prize and relations with Donald Trumpand the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. Uefa’s document also makes a number of allegations about potential conflicts of interests at Fifa, as well as repeating calls for a “genuinely independent” governance review.Apologetic Infantino ‘not fit’ to lead Fifa, claim European FA heads after meetingRead moreUefa’s latest intervention follows last week’s meeting of the Fifa council in Zurich, the first time it had gathered since the emergence of the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) controversy in July. Infantino listened to questions on FFE and other matters, but declined to provide substantive answers, instead asking council members to submit them in writing before their next meeting in Doha on 16 December.In a letter sent on Monday, Theodoridis wrote: “These explanations have not begun satisfactorily to address a number of fundamental questions raised by Council members.“Others remain unanswered, and the information and documentation requested have not been provided.“Following the invitation made during the meeting to submit our questions in writing, we therefore enclose a consolidated set of questions and requests for information.“We formally request a substantive written response to each question, together with all supporting documentation by Monday 2nd November. Any refusal to disclose information or documents should be justified individually, with a clear explanation of the specific grounds relied upon.“These questions require answers now. They cannot be deferred until the next meeting of theFifaCouncil – nor can future governance reforms substitute for scrutiny of decisions already taken and accountability for them.”View image in fullscreenAleksander Ceferin (centre), the Uefa president, and Theodore Theodoridis, the organisation’s general secretary, pictured in 2023.Photograph: Massimo Pinca/ReutersThe accompanying document and list of supplementary questions constitutes a damning takedown of Fifa’s leadership under Infantino, who, as it stands, is on course to be re-elected unopposed as president next year, although Uefa is increasingly hopeful of identifying a candidate to take him on before nominations close on 18 November.Uefa also wants answers on the processes behind other major decisions taken by Fifa over the past 12 months including moving the men’s World Cup draw to Washington DC from Las Vegas, the introduction of hydration breaks and the 27-minute half-time at the World Cup final.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“A series of decisions, transactions and interventions involving the Fifa President, the President of the United States and individuals associated with him raise serious questions concerning potential conflicts of interest, transparency and institutional accountability,” Uefa states.The amount Fifa is paying to rent office space in Trump Tower is also queried, as is a report in the Times last week that Infantino in 2024 “received substantial additional remuneration which was not disclosed in Fifa’s annual report”. Fifa has said it “does not pay a second salary to the Fifa president and complies with all reporting requirements in relation to compensation”.Uefa also raises concerns about March’s presidential election, specifically regarding the involvement of Bruno Chiomento, the chair of Fifa’s electoral committee. “We understand that Mr Chiomento has known the Fifa President for approximately 20 years and is regularly invited to Fifa events and competitions at Fifa’s expense,” Uefa’s document states. “We further understand that he attended the entire 2026 World Cup as an accredited individual, with his expenses covered by Fifa for more than five weeks.”Uefa has also requested a complete list of Fifa guests in VIP and VVIP areas at the World Cup final, on the grounds that “numerous guests were apparently given priority over Presidents of Member Associations and Secretaries General of Confederations”.Fifa has been contacted for comment.Explore more on these topicsFifaUefaFootball politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Semenyo’s eight-week injury absence leaves Manchester City short on cover for Haaland | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: The Ghana forward sustained a knee injury against Ipswich, as Maresca prepares to ring the changes against AEK Athens on Tuesday
Author: Will Unwin
Headline: The Ghana forward sustained a knee injury against Ipswich, as Maresca prepares to ring the changes against AEK Athens on Tuesday
Content: Antoine Semenyo had been viewed as the natural stand-in up front for Manchester City but he has been ruled out for eight weeks with a knee injury.Photograph: Michael Steele/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAntoine Semenyo had been viewed as the natural stand-in up front for Manchester City but he has been ruled out for eight weeks with a knee injury.Photograph: Michael Steele/Getty ImagesManchester CitySemenyo’s eight-week injury absence leaves Manchester City short on cover for HaalandGhana forward sustained knee injury against IpswichMaresca to ring changes against AEK Athens on TuesdayWill UnwinMon 19 Oct 2026 09.03 EDTLast modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 14.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAntoine Semenyo has been ruled out for eight weeks with a knee injury, leaving Enzo Maresca short of alternatives to Erling Haaland, who is a doubt for Manchester City’s Champions League game at home against AEK Athens on Tuesday.Semenyo limped offagainst Ipswich on Saturdayand Haaland hobbled off at full time with a foot injury. City are eager to get their European campaign back on track afterlosing against Paris Saint-Germainlast Wednesday. Maresca has said he will make changes and has admitted previously that Haaland will require resting at some point. Semenyo would have been the most obvious replacement but Phil Foden and Iliman Ndiaye could be utilised.“To replace Erling it’s always difficult but we have some different options; we’ll see tomorrow,” Maresca said. “To lose Antoine or any player for us is not good. Then in terms of Erling, we said that we can use Antoine as a 9 but also we have different players that we are going to try and to find new solutions.”Maresca witnessed a number of his players limp away from the win against Ipswich: Haaland, Semenyo, Mateo Kovacic, Matheus Nunes and Nico O’Reilly, who all featured at the World Cup. Maresca had made six changes, showing the need to rotate amid a hectic schedule of seven games in 21 days in October for City, many of whose players also had international commitments at the start of the month.“We try to manage all the players in the best way, try to keep them fit,” Maresca said. “Even sometimes things happen that you cannot control, like Antoine’s injury. We try to save him, we try to keep him fresh.”The fixtures mean it is difficult for Maresca to get training time as he tries to instil his style. “We try and do what we can on the pitch to go through a few things and tactics before the games,” the defender Marc Guéhi said. “It’s just a lot of recovery, sleep, to make sure the body is right for the next game,. It’s been enjoyable, to be honest; not to train, just playing games, which is fun.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionGuéhi was among the players who opted not to take a knee at the weekend as part of the Premier League’s “No Room For Racism” campaign. “I haven’t been taking the knee for a while now,” he said. “I’d always clap just because of what that actually signifies.” He wants greater action to combat racism in sport. “I hope we can do a bit more but we will just see. Hopefully the message is still getting out there, which is important.”Explore more on these topicsManchester CityEnzo MarescaErling HaalandnewsShareReuse this content

title: Konsa bullish about Arsenal’s Champions League hopes as Bayern clash looms | Arsenal | The Guardian
description: The centre-back has settled right in at Arsenal and is looking ‘to win everything’, starting with Wednesday’s duel against Harry Kane
Author: David Hytner
Headline: The centre-back has settled right in at Arsenal and is looking ‘to win everything’, starting with Wednesday’s duel against Harry Kane
Content: Ezri Konsa has been a mainstay for Arsenal since joining from Aston Villa in the summer.Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenEzri Konsa has been a mainstay for Arsenal since joining from Aston Villa in the summer.Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesArsenalKonsa bullish about Arsenal’s Champions League hopes as Bayern clash loomsCentre-back has settled right in at Arsenal and is looking ‘to win everything’, starting with Wednesday’s duel against Harry KaneDavid HytnerMon 19 Oct 2026 10.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 13.37 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFor Ezri Konsa, it was just a wonderfully satisfying challenge. The Nottingham Forest striker Liam Delap had stolen in behind him up the inside left channel on Sunday. There were 93 minutes gone,Arsenalwere 1-0 up and it was now or never for Forest. Konsa decreed that it would be never, curving his covering run back, matching Delap for pace and stretching into the perfect block tackle.So,another win for Arsenal: their 10th in 11 matches this season. Another clean sheet. And for Konsa, a continuation of what has been a dreamlike couple of months. Do points-saving last-minute challenges mean more when the defender is actually a fan of the club, too? Basically, yes.Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s actionRead more“I’ve been asked this a lot,” Konsa says with a smile, when the subject of his boyhood allegiance is raised. “And, yes, I was [an Arsenal supporter]. I had a lot of Arsenal kits when I was younger. You dream of playing for big clubs like this. When you’re a kid, you see the likes of Arsenal, growing up, and the amount of quality players they’ve had throughout the years and to be here – and not only to be here but to be here with close friends – makes it even more special.”Konsa is talking about Eberechi Eze, in particular; another boyhood Arsenal fan, with whom he is especially tight. Many supporters have seen the clip of Eze greeting Konsa at the training ground after the latter had completedhis £51m move from Aston Villaand how they crack up with laughter before embracing. It is infectious. But Konsa knows a clutch of other Arsenal players from England duty – Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka, Noni Madueke, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Ben White – and he credits them with helping him to settle in.The 28-year-old’s adaptation has been quick and it has needed to bewith William Saliba injured. After making his Arsenal debutas a substitute at Villa– Konsa’s scriptwriters have been hard at work – he has played in every minute of the club’s Premier League and Champions League matches. The victory at Forest, where Arsenal had drawn 0-0 in each of the previous two seasons, was significant.It was not a performance of any attacking pace or spark. Perhaps it made the points feel more precious.“We hadn’t won here in two seasons, the boss was going on about it,” Konsa says. “It’s something we wanted to change as players and these are the games you have to win. If you want to win titles, you have to come away to tough places like this and get three points.”View image in fullscreenEzri Konsa does battle with Liam Delap during Arsenal’s 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianThings are about to get even more interesting for Konsa and Arsenal because on Wednesdaythey face Bayern Munich at the Allianz Arenain the Champions League. “It’s against my international teammate as well,” Konsa says, and he is straight into an appreciation of Harry Kane, the England captain, who has been on fire since joining Bayern from Tottenham in 2023. Kane’s scoring record for the club bears repeating: 155 goals in 157 appearances.Konsa has a good record against Kane, having faced him seven times, six of them for Villa against Spurs. The seventh and most recent came in October 2024 when Konsa was in the Villa team thatbeat Kane’s Bayern 1-0 at Villa Parkin the Champions League. It was Villa’s first home match in the competition for 41 years. The defender has four wins against Kane’s teams and three losses. Kane has only scored twice against him, both from penalties.“The Villa-Bayern game … to beat them at home and keep a clean sheet … it was very special for the players and the fans,” Konsa says. “I don’t really look much at those kind of stats [against individual players] but I am relishing the challenge.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe dynamics against Bayern appear different for Konsa this time. It was a famous victory for Villa that night, in part because of the tie’s history; the club beat Bayern 1-0 in the 1982 European Cup final. Villa were underdogs as they felt their way back into Europe’s elite competition. Arsenal will kick off as Bayern’s equals and among the favourites to win the tournament,having lost on penalties to Paris Saint-Germainin last season’s final.Konsa won the first trophy of his career a week before that when he was in the Villa team thatdefeated Freiburg in the Europa League final. He says he has felt the determination of the Arsenal squad to go one step further in Europe.“One hundred per cent,” Konsa says. “As players, the standards we have, the goals we have … we want to win everything – the Champions League, the Prem. Whatever trophies are in front of us. When I came to Arsenal, I wanted to win. I was hungry to win. Last season I got my hands on the Europa League and this season I want more.”Explore more on these topicsArsenalfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Sarina Wiegman signs contract extension to stay as England women head coach until 2029 | England women's football team | The Guardian
description: Sarina Wiegman has the chance to lead the Lionesses to three European championship titles in a row after extending her deal by two years
Author: Suzanne Wrack
Headline: Sarina Wiegman has the chance to lead the Lionesses to three European championship titles in a row after extending her deal by two years
Content: Sarina Wiegman celebrates with Leah Williamson after England win the Euro 2025 final.Photograph: Maja Hitij/UEFA/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenSarina Wiegman celebrates with Leah Williamson after England win the Euro 2025 final.Photograph: Maja Hitij/UEFA/Getty ImagesEngland women's football teamSarina Wiegman signs contract extension to stay as England women head coach until 2029Wiegman says she ‘cannot think of a better job in football’She can target three European titles in row with LionessesSuzanne WrackMon 19 Oct 2026 06.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 15.10 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSarina Wiegman has extended her contract to continue as the head coach of England women for Euro 2029. Her deal was due to expire after the World Cup next summer and this extension gives her the chance to lead the Lionesses to three European championship titles in a row.Wiegman, whotook on the role in September 2021, also led her native Netherlands side to European Championship glory in 2017 and has reached the final of the past five major tournaments, twice finishing as a World Cup runner-up.“I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football,” Wiegman said. “Working for a world-class organisation like the FA, and alongside so many people dedicated to winning England teams and the growth of our game, excites me every day.”Quick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.England will reach the World Cup finals, to be held in Brazil in June and July, if they come through a two-leg playoff against Ukraine for which they are heavy favourites. “My main concern right now is absolutely the World Cup, and helping this squad realise their potential in the years to come,” Wiegman said.This is Wiegman’s second contract extension with England and opens the possibility that she could coach Team GB at the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles should the team qualify. Wiegman, who turns 57 next Monday, will continue to be assisted by Janneke Bijl, Arvid Smit and Darren Ward.“Sarina is an incredible coach with an unparalleled record in major tournaments and I am so happy to continue to work with her for the next Euro cycle,” the Football Association’s chief executive, Mark Bullingham, said.Wiegman had refused to be drawn on questions over her future before England’s two games against Greece during the recent international break, but the Chelsea midfielder Keira Walsh last week said “obviously I’d want her to stay” when asked about the head coach’s future.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“Sarina’s the boss, I would never ask her those questions, but I think everyone in England would love her to stay,” Walsh said. “I’ve played a lot of games for her and I really appreciate her as a manager.”Explore more on these topicsEngland women's football teamSarina WiegmanThe FAWomen's footballnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘Like a family’: De Zerbi credits players’ talk and bonding trip for improving Tottenham | Tottenham Hotspur | The Guardian
description: Roberto De Zerbi revealed a players’ meeting has helped his Tottenham side play with more togetherness
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: Roberto De Zerbi revealed a players’ meeting has helped his Tottenham side play with more togetherness
Content: Tottenham’s James Maddison celebrates his first goal since May 2025 with Omar Marmoush (left), who scored the second goal.Photograph: Rob Newell/CameraSport/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenTottenham’s James Maddison celebrates his first goal since May 2025 with Omar Marmoush (left), who scored the second goal.Photograph: Rob Newell/CameraSport/Getty ImagesTottenham Hotspur‘Like a family’: De Zerbi credits players’ talk and bonding trip for improving TottenhamSpurs off bottom after first win against CoventryLampard unhappy Marmoush goal stoodJacob Steinbergat the Tottenham Hotspur StadiumMon 19 Oct 2026 18.14 EDTLast modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 18.28 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRoberto De Zerbi said that Tottenham are playing with more togetherness after holding a clear-the-air meeting before their recent game with Manchester United.Spurs went on to draw 1-1 with 10 men against United and are out of the bottom three after beating Coventry 3-1 at home on Monday night. De Zerbi felt the performance against Coventry could have been better but was happy with his side’s attitude as they claimed their first Premier League win of the season.Davies ensures Spurs off the bottom after first win of season against CoventryRead more“It’s important,” the Spurs manager said. “The result is important but most important, two things. First one, we are able to realise we can win a game like other teams in the Premier League. The second thing, if we put [in] something from ourselves like we have done in the last two weeks. The day before Old Trafford we had a big meeting and spoke about the situation. We can’t accept and can’t move on if we don’t accept responsibility.”De Zerbi took his squad to Marbella for a bonding trip and warm weather training last week. “This week has been important because we spend time together and want to be like a family,” he said. “During the game if you have a problem and there is a tough situation you have to play for your friend and your brother, not like 11 robot players on the pitch.”Spurs took the lead when James Maddison marked his first start in 536 days with a brilliant goal. Coventry equalised through Jack Rudoni but Omar Marmoush responded with his first goal since leaving Manchester City and Ben Davies sealed the result.Spurs are up to 16th and De Zerbi was happy that Maddison’s first goal since May 2025 was joined by Dejan Kulusevski coming off the bench to make his first appearance since suffering a serious knee injury in the same month.“They are different players,” De Zerbi said. “Different talent, different experience, different personality. With them in the dressing room there is another atmosphere.”Frank Lampard was happy with Coventry’s fight but was surprised that Marmoush’s goal was not ruled out after the Egyptian elbowed Milan van Ewijk. “I did think that,” Coventry’s manager said. “If you roll and your elbow is that high and it connects with Milan, I thought VAR would cancel it.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionLampard was optimistic about his side. “It was a really big display,” he said. “3-1 changes the view at the end of the game. At 2-1 we were pushing.”Explore more on these topicsTottenham HotspurCoventry CityRoberto De ZerbiFrank LampardnewsShareReuse this content
